newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to get tough on corruption.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to get tough on corruption.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday it was stepping up its fight against corruption through stricter punishments and the possible establishment of a powerful anti-graft board.
Justice Minister Nguyen Dinh Loc was quoted by official media as saying proposed changes to the criminal law would define bribery and set out punishments, including the use of the death penalty.
He said the Justice Ministry had been appointed to examine a beefing up of the police and justice system or the setting up a nationwide anti-corruption committee.

"...such a committee should be given much freedom to operate independently by the government in tandem with the adoption of a comprehensive anti-corruption law," he was quoted as saying by the English-language Vietnam News.
Corruption is endemic in Vietnam. Earlier this year, a Hong Kong-based consultancy ranked the country as one of the most graft-ridden in Asia.
But the issue has taken on growing political tones in recent months reflected by increased coverage of major corruption cases in Vietnam's domestic media.

Communist Party chief Do Muoi was quoted by Tuesday's Saigon Giai Phong newspaper as criticising party cells operating within businesses for failing to act as an effective vanguard against the problem.
"It's time for us to combat corruption not by talking about it, but by activities, very strong activities," he was quoted as saying.
